decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete message-247 MODIFY covering the uninterrupted liquid test, both stations and spouts, several minutes without leaks, and the dry-underside inspection.
The source changes leak-test acceptance conditions but does not change splash prevention or operating-cleanliness behavior.
Both stations were already required to run simultaneously; the source merely includes that existing behavior in the final leak test.
Requiring liquid to dispense through both spouts does not change their geometry, mounting, orientation, material, appearance, or pour direction.
Briefly showing the underside for dryness is an inspection step and does not change the requirement that internal components remain accessible for service.
The favorable spin-test observation does not modify structural-stability or vibration-control requirements, and implementation status must not be propagated as a MODIFY.
The source requires dispensing during a leak test but does not change the button control, valve mechanism, flow behavior, sequence, or drip constraints.
The liquid test and dry-underside inspection do not change dispensing-path removal, cleaning, sanitation-access, or liquid-trap requirements.
A dry underside is a leak-containment check, but the source does not change the existing requirement to keep liquid from electrical components or establish a distinct electrical-isolation condition.
Dispensing through both spouts during testing does not change platform height, footprint, cup size, or clearance behavior.
Several minutes of operation is specified as part of the leak test, not as a new motor-durability or maximum-speed duty requirement.
The final liquid test does not change the system-layout, CAD, documentation, motor-accommodation, or component-clearance deliverables.
